A full run is split into eight shards, one CI job each, so the run stays inside the nightly budget at the 4,600-repository target. Locally:

npm run validate:public-repos -- --shard 2/8 --offline
npm run corpus:merge -- --dir shard-reports --output corpus-result.json
have selected the entries. Every entry belongs to exactly one shard and membership is stable for a given corpus order, so two runs pick the same split. The JSON report records
A shard is not a full run: it says

files, refuses anything that is not the complete set of verify-mode shards, checks every repository against its pinned commit exactly once, merges in corpus order, enforces the floors, and writes the single full report the artifact and the job summary expect. It applies the shard budgets described below.
Each repository is scanned in its own child process with an old-generation heap limit: 1024 MB by default,
to change it. A repository that exceeds the limit, throws, or runs longer than its scan timeout (300 s by default,

, counts its expected findings as missing, and the run carries on to the next repository; the run fails at the end. A fetch that exhausts its retries is recorded the same way, so one repository can neither crash the shard nor hide behind a missing report.

A budget overrun never fails the run; correctness is decided by false positives, false negatives, and failed scans.

The current limits are 600 s and 500 MB per shard, measured rather than guessed. At the 4,600 target a shard owns about 575 repositories, 8.3 times today's 70. A warm shard of 70 takes about 13 s (about two minutes at the target). A cold shard of 70 measured 107.1 s and fetched 53.3 MB here (another run of the same shard took 319.5 s on the same connection), which is about 440 MB for one target shard; decision 0015 measured 112 repositories cold in 49.8 s on an ordinary connection. The 600 s and 500 MB limits leave room for that spread, and the weekly job's timeout is 20 minutes. Tighten the budget in a pull request when a faster fetch strategy lands, and raise it only with a stated reason and a measurement.
One hung connection must not hold a run. Each fetch passes git's low-speed abort (

entry for that repository while the rest of the shard continues. At the end of every run the five slowest fetches print as
